summary.en: Libyan armed forces keep conducting extrajudicial executions, breaking a 15-year moratorium, while eastern authorities hold dozens of detainees at risk of execution. Haftar's forces have signed a strategic cooperation protocol with Niger, and a RPG shell caused a factory blast in Sebha that killed two people. Jordan and Libya discussed joint military training, coordination and exchange of defense expertise, and an armed group shut the Hamada pipeline valve, halting crude supplies to the Al-Zawiya refinery. 2 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Libyske væpnede styrker fortsetter med utenrettslige henrettelser, og bryter et 15‑årig moratorium, mens østlige myndigheter holder dusinvis av fanger i fare for henrettelse. Haftars styrker har signert en strategisk samarbeidsprotokoll med Niger, og en RPG-granat forårsaket en fabrikkeksplosjon i Sebha som drepte to personer. Jordan og Libya diskuterte felles militær trening, koordinering og utveksling av forsvarsekspertise, og en væpnet gruppe stengte ventilen på Hamada-røret, noe som stoppet råoljeleveranser til Al-Zawiya-raffineriet. 2 kamprelaterte dødsfall i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Libyan crisis
background.extract: The Libyan crisis is the current humanitarian crisis and political-military instability occurring in Libya, beginning with the Arab Spring protests of 2011, which led to two civil wars, foreign military intervention, and the ousting and killing of Muammar Gaddafi. The first civil war's aftermath and proliferation of armed groups led to violence and instability across the country, which erupted into renewed civil war in 2014. The second war lasted until 23 October 2020, when all parties agreed to a permanent ceasefire and negotiations.
